method: COMPILED FROM 2 SOURCES. S1: QUOTED from Rostampour N, Dalili S, Moravej H, et al., Orphanet Journal of Rare Diseases 'Comprehensive Iranian guidelines for the diagnosis and management of maple syrup urine disease: an evidence- and consensus- based approach' (vol. 20, article 8, published 7 January 2025), 20 claims; LICENCE: CC BY 4.0 (read at Europe PMC fullTextXML <license> element for PMC11707931 ('licensed under a Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International License')). S2: PARAPHRASED AND HASH-ANCHORED from Genetic Metabolic Dietitians International (GMDI) and the Southeast Regional Genetics Network (SERN), Management Guidelines Portal 'MSUD Nutrition Management Guidelines, Second Edition (v2.1)' (second edition October 2024, v2.1, updated March 2026), 10 claims; LICENCE: No licence or reproduction permission stated on the portal (disclaimer page read); treated as all rights reserved (read at https://managementguidelines.net/guidelines.php/148/disclaim/0/0/MSUD and the portal footer). Verify each source separately: verify.py --source <file> --only-source S<n>. Edition 2.0 adds S2, the GMDI/SERN MSUD nutrition guideline (second edition of Frazier et al. 2014), read on GMDI's own free portal: recommendation, monitoring and table pages fetched and tag-stripped into one text. Its Tables 4 and 6 survived as text and are anchored. The S1 claims and fragments are unchanged. Table rows appended with pmc_text.py --append-tables (2026-09-24); claims from S1 Table 1 (phenotypes) and Table 3 (daily intakes by age). S1 Tables 2 and 4 (ragged rows) were not extracted.

claims.claim: **Classic MSUD presents in the first weeks of life** after feeds begin: poor feeding, vomiting, drowsiness, then lethargy and falling consciousness; coma and cerebral oedema follow. Variant forms present later, triggered by illness, fasting or surgery.
claims.source_text: Classic MSUD phenotype typically manifests in newborns, whereas, the other variants may present at any time during infancy or childhood, usually triggered by episodes of stress, such as concurrent illness, fasting, or surgery. The patients with classic type of MSUD are normal at birth, but they present clinical manifestation including poor feeding, vomiting, drowsiness, gradually leading to irritability, lethargy, and a decrease in consciousness after breast and formula feeding, in the first weeks of life.
claims.locator: Rostampour N, Dalili S, Moravej H, et al., Orphanet Journal of Rare Diseases, 'Comprehensive Iranian guidelines for the diagnosis and management of maple syrup urine disease: an evidence- and consensus- based approach', vol. 20, article 8, published 7 January 2025, https://doi.org/10.1186/s13023-025-03533-6, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Suspect MSUD** with an abnormal newborn screen, or with refractory hypoglycaemia, seizures, hypertonia, 'boxing and bicycling' movements or a maple-syrup odour.
claims.source_text: MSUD should be suspected in asymptomatic patients with abnormal neonatal screening and/or symptomatic cases with clinical manifestations suspicious to MSUD. These manifestations include metabolic acidosis with a normal anion gap, convulsion, hypoglycemia refractory to treatment with or without symptoms, hypertonia, boxing& bicycling, and sometimes peculiar odor of maple syrup in urine or body
claims.locator: Rostampour N, Dalili S, Moravej H, et al., Orphanet Journal of Rare Diseases, 'Comprehensive Iranian guidelines for the diagnosis and management of maple syrup urine disease: an evidence- and consensus- based approach', vol. 20, article 8, published 7 January 2025, https://doi.org/10.1186/s13023-025-03533-6, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Positive screen (leucine + isoleucine > 250 nmol/L, or ratio > 3): confirm with plasma amino acids and alloisoleucine; if BCAAs are clearly high and/or alloisoleucine > 2 nmol/ml, treat immediately.** Never give a protein challenge to make the diagnosis.
claims.source_text: If the screening is positive (i.e. leucine + isoleucine > 250 nmol/L or its ratio to alanine and phenylalanine concentrations > 3), the neonate needs confirmatory biochemical testing with measurement of plasma amino acids and alloisoleucine. If BCAAs are significantly elevated and/or alloisoleucine > 2 nmol/ml, treatment should be initiated immediately. … Neonates and infants who are suspicious of MSUD should never be challenged with higher than normal protein intake for diagnostic purposes.
claims.locator: Rostampour N, Dalili S, Moravej H, et al., Orphanet Journal of Rare Diseases, 'Comprehensive Iranian guidelines for the diagnosis and management of maple syrup urine disease: an evidence- and consensus- based approach', vol. 20, article 8, published 7 January 2025, https://doi.org/10.1186/s13023-025-03533-6, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Molecular genetic testing is the preferred confirmation, but do not delay treatment waiting for it.**
claims.source_text: Molecular genetic testing is the preferred confirmatory test for MSUD. … Every patient who is highly suspicious of MSUD according to plasma amino acid levels should be treated immediately. Management of the patients should not be delayed while awaiting the molecular genetic result
claims.locator: Rostampour N, Dalili S, Moravej H, et al., Orphanet Journal of Rare Diseases, 'Comprehensive Iranian guidelines for the diagnosis and management of maple syrup urine disease: an evidence- and consensus- based approach', vol. 20, article 8, published 7 January 2025, https://doi.org/10.1186/s13023-025-03533-6, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Phenotypes (S1 Table 1), by residual BCKD activity:** classic, newborn onset, 0-2%, crises in the newborn period and with catabolic stress; intermediate, infancy to childhood, 3-30%, crises with catabolic stress; intermittent, 5-20%, normal BCAAs when well but episodic decompensations that can be severe; thiamine-responsive, 2-40%, better leucine tolerance with thiamine alongside diet; E3 deficiency, newborn, with persistent lactic acidosis, high pyruvate and alanine and only moderately raised BCAAs.
claims.source_text: [Table 1 row 1] Clinical phenotypes: Classic · Age of onset 1: Newborn · Severity: Moderate to severe · Acute metabolic decompensation: Yes (newborn period and with catabolic stress) · Response t0 thiamine: No · Clinical features: Maple syrup odor of cerumen Poor feeding Irritability, lethargy Opisthotonus Focal dystonia "Fencing," "bicycling" Obtundation, coma Central respiratory failure · Biochemical signs: ↑ BCAAs in plasma ↑ plasma alloisoleucine ↑ BCKAs in urine Ketonuria · % Residual BCKD activity 2: 0-2% … [Table 1 row 2] Clinical phenotypes: Intermediate · Age of onset 1: Infancy to childhood · Severity: Moderate to severe · Acute metabolic decompensation: Yes (with catabolic stress) · Response t0 thiamine: No · Clinical features: Maple syrup odor of cerumen Poor growth Poor feeding Irritability Developmental delays Encephalopathy during illness Neurologic symptoms · Biochemical signs: Similar to classic phenotype, though quantitatively less severe · % Residual BCKD activity 2: 3-30% … [Table 1 row 3] Clinical phenotypes: Intermittent · Age of onset 1: Infancy to childhood, or adulthood (rare) · Severity: Mild to moderate · Acute metabolic decompensation: Rare · Response t0 thiamine: No · Clinical features: Normal early growth & development Learning disability Neurological symptoms Episodic decompensations that can be severe · Biochemical signs: Normal BCAAs when the patient is well similar to the classic biochemical profile during illness · % Residual BCKD activity 2: 5-20% … [Table 1 row 4] Clinical phenotypes: Thiamine responsive · Age of onset 1: Infancy to childhood · Severity: Moderate · Acute metabolic decompensation: Rare · Response t0 thiamine: In conjunction with dietary therapy · Clinical features: Similar to intermediate phenotype · Biochemical signs: Improvement of leucine tolerance & biochemical profile with thiamine therapy · % Residual BCKD activity 2: 2-40% … [Table 1 row 5] Clinical phenotypes: E3 ² · Age of onset 1: Newborn · Severity: Moderate · Acute metabolic decompensation: rare · Response t0 thiamine: No · Clinical features: hypotonia and developmental delay · Biochemical signs: persistent lactic acidosis with high levels of plasma pyruvate and alanine. Plasma BCAA concentrations are moderately increased. · % Residual BCKD activity 2: Not known
claims.locator: Rostampour N, Dalili S, Moravej H, et al., Orphanet Journal of Rare Diseases, 'Comprehensive Iranian guidelines for the diagnosis and management of maple syrup urine disease: an evidence- and consensus- based approach', vol. 20, article 8, published 7 January 2025, https://doi.org/10.1186/s13023-025-03533-6, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Aim to lower leucine by 500 to 1000 µmoles/L/day;** symptomatic patients should preferably go to PICU.
claims.source_text: The principle goal of treatment in these patients is the reduction of the leucine level by 500 to 1000 µmoles/L/day []. Symptomatic patients should preferably be admitted to the PICU.
claims.locator: Rostampour N, Dalili S, Moravej H, et al., Orphanet Journal of Rare Diseases, 'Comprehensive Iranian guidelines for the diagnosis and management of maple syrup urine disease: an evidence- and consensus- based approach', vol. 20, article 8, published 7 January 2025, https://doi.org/10.1186/s13023-025-03533-6, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Stop natural protein for 24 to 48 h (up to 72 h in adults);** give 1.25–1.5 times maintenance IV fluid as 10–12.5% dextrose in normal saline, with Intralipid 1–2 g/kg/day for extra calories.
claims.source_text: Natural Protein intake should be stopped for 24 to 48 h [, ]. This period could be extended to 24 to 72 h in adults []. We recommend 1.25-1.5 times intravenous maintenance. Fluids should be given as 10-12.5% dextrose in normal saline … Intralipid solution can be used with a dose of 1-2 g/kg/day to provide more calories
claims.locator: Rostampour N, Dalili S, Moravej H, et al., Orphanet Journal of Rare Diseases, 'Comprehensive Iranian guidelines for the diagnosis and management of maple syrup urine disease: an evidence- and consensus- based approach', vol. 20, article 8, published 7 January 2025, https://doi.org/10.1186/s13023-025-03533-6, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Check glucose every 4 to 6 h, keeping it between 100 and 160 mg/dl;** insulin infusion if hyperglycaemic. Keep sodium between 138 and 145 mEq/L and avoid osmolality falling more than 5 mOsm/kg H2O per day.
claims.source_text: It is necessary to check blood sugar every 4 to 6 h. The goal is to maintain blood sugar between 100 and 160 mg/dl []. In case of hyperglycemia, insulin infusion can be started … Serum sodium levels should be maintained between 138 and 145 mEq/L. … avoid serum osmolality from decreasing > 5 mOsm/kg H2O per day
claims.locator: Rostampour N, Dalili S, Moravej H, et al., Orphanet Journal of Rare Diseases, 'Comprehensive Iranian guidelines for the diagnosis and management of maple syrup urine disease: an evidence- and consensus- based approach', vol. 20, article 8, published 7 January 2025, https://doi.org/10.1186/s13023-025-03533-6, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Give BCAA-free amino acids (2–3.5 g/ kg /day if IV is available) with isoleucine and valine supplements;** once oral feeding is possible, run BCAA-free formula continuously by NG tube.
claims.source_text: Protein as BCAA-free amino acids with a dose of 2-3.5 g/ kg /day (if the intravenous form is available) together with isoleucine and valine supplements (20 to 120 mg/kg/day titrate to plasma level remains between 400 and 800 µmole/L) were recommended for leucine reduction [, ]. For patients that can tolerate oral feeding, continuous feeding of BCAA-free MSUD formula with an NG tube in the range of 30 to 60 cc per hour (0.7-1.2 kcal/ml) should be started
claims.locator: Rostampour N, Dalili S, Moravej H, et al., Orphanet Journal of Rare Diseases, 'Comprehensive Iranian guidelines for the diagnosis and management of maple syrup urine disease: an evidence- and consensus- based approach', vol. 20, article 8, published 7 January 2025, https://doi.org/10.1186/s13023-025-03533-6, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Consider dialysis for leucine above 1100 µmole/L and/or rapidly progressing neurological signs;** short-course continuous haemodialysis beats peritoneal dialysis.
claims.source_text: Dialysis should be considered in the case of leucine of more than 1100 µmole/L and/or rapid onset of neurological symptoms []. The use of short-course continuous hemodialysis is more effective than peritoneal dialysis and veno-venous hemofiltration
claims.locator: Rostampour N, Dalili S, Moravej H, et al., Orphanet Journal of Rare Diseases, 'Comprehensive Iranian guidelines for the diagnosis and management of maple syrup urine disease: an evidence- and consensus- based approach', vol. 20, article 8, published 7 January 2025, https://doi.org/10.1186/s13023-025-03533-6, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Treat triggers** (infection, trauma, dehydration) with a low threshold for empiric antibiotics. Thiamine-responsive patients take 50–200 mg daily, IV if oral is not tolerated.
claims.source_text: Triggering factors including infection, trauma, and dehydration should be treated. A low clinical threshold for empiric administration of antibiotics when signs of infection are present should be considered. … Some patients are treated with thiamine as thiamine responsive with a dose of 50-200 mg daily
claims.locator: Rostampour N, Dalili S, Moravej H, et al., Orphanet Journal of Rare Diseases, 'Comprehensive Iranian guidelines for the diagnosis and management of maple syrup urine disease: an evidence- and consensus- based approach', vol. 20, article 8, published 7 January 2025, https://doi.org/10.1186/s13023-025-03533-6, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Cerebral oedema needs ICU care;** options include mannitol, hypertonic (3%) saline and furosemide, holding sodium at 138 to 145 mEq/L.
claims.source_text: 1- Cerebral edema: When intracranial hypertension occurs, the patient should be admitted to the ICU and neurological consultation should be done. Symptomatic hypo-osmolality or worsening signs of intracranial hypertension should be treated with the following options including mannitol 0.5-1 g/kg/dose, hypertonic (3%) saline: 2-3 mEq/kg/dose and furosemide 0.5-1 mg/kg/dose. In cases of moderate to severe encephalopathy, we start NaCl drip 5 to 15 mEq/kg/day, to the extent that serum osmolality is maintained between 290 and 300 mOsm/kg H2O, serum sodium is maintained in the range of 138 to 145 mEq/L
claims.locator: Rostampour N, Dalili S, Moravej H, et al., Orphanet Journal of Rare Diseases, 'Comprehensive Iranian guidelines for the diagnosis and management of maple syrup urine disease: an evidence- and consensus- based approach', vol. 20, article 8, published 7 January 2025, https://doi.org/10.1186/s13023-025-03533-6, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **GMDI crisis nutrition:** up to 150% of usual energy; extra BCAA-free protein to replace the intact protein withdrawn; fluid up to 150ml/kg while watching electrolytes and for cerebral oedema; electrolytes and insulin as needed. Use parenteral nutrition (BCAA-free amino acids, lipid, glucose), alone or with feeds, when energy needs cannot otherwise be met.
claims.locator: Genetic Metabolic Dietitians International (GMDI) and the Southeast Regional Genetics Network (SERN), Management Guidelines Portal, 'MSUD Nutrition Management Guidelines, Second Edition (v2.1)', second edition October 2024, v2.1, updated March 2026, https://managementguidelines.net/guidelines.php/148/MSUD, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Give isoleucine and valine even when they already read 200-400 µmol/L,** because they help bring leucine down. Restart intact protein (or a complete amino acid mix) as leucine nears the top of its range, 200 µmol/L at 5 years or under and 300 µmol/L above 5; in reports this was usually within 48-72 hours.
claims.locator: Genetic Metabolic Dietitians International (GMDI) and the Southeast Regional Genetics Network (SERN), Management Guidelines Portal, 'MSUD Nutrition Management Guidelines, Second Edition (v2.1)', second edition October 2024, v2.1, updated March 2026, https://managementguidelines.net/guidelines.php/148/MSUD, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Breast milk can be the infant's intact-protein source** (mean leucine about 1 mg/mL) if the mother's supply is adequate and the baby's growth, clinical state and bloods are checked often.
claims.locator: Genetic Metabolic Dietitians International (GMDI) and the Southeast Regional Genetics Network (SERN), Management Guidelines Portal, 'MSUD Nutrition Management Guidelines, Second Edition (v2.1)', second edition October 2024, v2.1, updated March 2026, https://managementguidelines.net/guidelines.php/148/MSUD, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Start the sick-day protocol at the first symptoms;** home care only suits fever under 38.5 °C, tolerated oral or NG feeds, no frequent vomiting or severe diarrhoea, and no neurological signs. Otherwise admit.
claims.source_text: The sick day protocol should be started as soon as appearing of the first symptoms of the disease. This protocol is applicable only for minor diseases that can be treated at home. Mild cases of increased catabolism that can be treated on an outpatient basis include fever under 38.5 °C, tolerance of oral feeding or NG tube feeding, without frequent vomiting or severe diarrhea, and absence of neurological symptoms such as consciousness changes, restlessness, and hypotonia. Otherwise, the patient needs hospitalization and intravenous treatment.
claims.locator: Rostampour N, Dalili S, Moravej H, et al., Orphanet Journal of Rare Diseases, 'Comprehensive Iranian guidelines for the diagnosis and management of maple syrup urine disease: an evidence- and consensus- based approach', vol. 20, article 8, published 7 January 2025, https://doi.org/10.1186/s13023-025-03533-6, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **At home:** cut leucine by 50–100%, reduce or stop natural protein, raise BCAA-free formula to 120% of usual, give extra isoleucine and valine (20–40 mg/kg/day each), frequent carbohydrate drinks, and reassess every two hours.
claims.source_text: The consumption of leucine should be reduced by 50-100%. The consumption of natural protein should be reduced or stopped. The consumption of BCAA-free formula should be increased to the 120% of the usual consumption. Increasing the consumption of isoleucine and valine supplements (20-40 mg/kg/day of each). … Re-evaluation of clinical changes every two hours
claims.locator: Rostampour N, Dalili S, Moravej H, et al., Orphanet Journal of Rare Diseases, 'Comprehensive Iranian guidelines for the diagnosis and management of maple syrup urine disease: an evidence- and consensus- based approach', vol. 20, article 8, published 7 January 2025, https://doi.org/10.1186/s13023-025-03533-6, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **GMDI sick-day plan for mild illness:** replace 50-100% of intact protein with extra BCAA-free medical food for 24-48 hours, keep up fluids, add non-protein energy and monitor closely, following a written plan for that patient.
claims.locator: Genetic Metabolic Dietitians International (GMDI) and the Southeast Regional Genetics Network (SERN), Management Guidelines Portal, 'MSUD Nutrition Management Guidelines, Second Edition (v2.1)', second edition October 2024, v2.1, updated March 2026, https://managementguidelines.net/guidelines.php/148/MSUD, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Plasma targets:** leucine 75–200 µmol/L up to 5 years and 75–300 µmol/L above 5 years; valine and isoleucine 200 to 400 µmol/L. The diet is lifelong.
claims.source_text: Plasma Leucine level: children ≤ 5 years of age: 75-200 µmol/L and children > 5 years of age: 75-300 µmol/L. Plasma valine and isoleucine levels: 200 to 400 µmol/L … Therefore, the patients should be on a diet their whole life.
claims.locator: Rostampour N, Dalili S, Moravej H, et al., Orphanet Journal of Rare Diseases, 'Comprehensive Iranian guidelines for the diagnosis and management of maple syrup urine disease: an evidence- and consensus- based approach', vol. 20, article 8, published 7 January 2025, https://doi.org/10.1186/s13023-025-03533-6, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **When stable, check BCAAs every 1 to 2 weeks until 5 years, every 2 to 4 weeks until 12 years, then monthly;** give iron, zinc, calcium, selenium, vitamin A and D supplements.
claims.source_text: In stable patients, monitoring of blood or plasma BCAA is done every 1 to 2 weeks until 5 years of age, then every 2 to 4 weeks until 12 years of age, and monthly afterward … Essential supplements such as Fe, zinc, calcium, selenium, vitamin A, and vitamin D should be given to the patients.
claims.locator: Rostampour N, Dalili S, Moravej H, et al., Orphanet Journal of Rare Diseases, 'Comprehensive Iranian guidelines for the diagnosis and management of maple syrup urine disease: an evidence- and consensus- based approach', vol. 20, article 8, published 7 January 2025, https://doi.org/10.1186/s13023-025-03533-6, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **New infant:** admit to start treatment; stop breast milk and formula briefly, give 3 g/kg/day BCAA-free protein equivalent in a high-energy feed, then reintroduce leucine from formula or expressed breast milk once plasma leucine is < 800 µmol/L. Breastfeeding on demand is possible after a measured BCAA-free feed.
claims.source_text: Every infant with MSUD should be hospitalized at the beginning of treatment so that his/her clinical evaluation is done completely his/her tolerance to nutritional recommendations is evaluated … Breastfeeding (BF) and infant formula (leucine source) are stopped temporarily. Oral or Enteral feeding should be commenced early. Provide 3 g/kg/day BCAA-free protein equivalent. … Leucine is given from standard infant formula/ expressed breastmilk (EBM) when plasma leucine is < 800 µmol/L. … Infants can then be breastfed on demand, but always with a measured quantity of BCAA‐free infant formula first
claims.locator: Rostampour N, Dalili S, Moravej H, et al., Orphanet Journal of Rare Diseases, 'Comprehensive Iranian guidelines for the diagnosis and management of maple syrup urine disease: an evidence- and consensus- based approach', vol. 20, article 8, published 7 January 2025, https://doi.org/10.1186/s13023-025-03533-6, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Non-classic forms need less:** intermediate MSUD needs leucine restriction ± BCAA-free amino acids and an emergency regimen; intermittent MSUD may need only moderate protein restriction; thiamine-responsive patients also take thiamine.
claims.source_text: For intermediate MSUD, leucine restriction ± branched chain free amino acids and an ER are necessary. For intermittent MSUD, may only require moderate protein restriction (no branched chain free amino acids) and an ER. Also, in thiamin-responsive phenotype patients, leucine restriction ± branched chain free amino acids and thiamin supplementation and an ER
claims.locator: Rostampour N, Dalili S, Moravej H, et al., Orphanet Journal of Rare Diseases, 'Comprehensive Iranian guidelines for the diagnosis and management of maple syrup urine disease: an evidence- and consensus- based approach', vol. 20, article 8, published 7 January 2025, https://doi.org/10.1186/s13023-025-03533-6, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Liver transplant** allows a normal diet but is reserved for patients uncontrolled on diet with multiple attacks.
claims.source_text: Liver transplant is promising and leads to normal diet toleration. Due to the various side effects, it is only done in patients who cannot be controlled with diet and have multiple attacks.
claims.locator: Rostampour N, Dalili S, Moravej H, et al., Orphanet Journal of Rare Diseases, 'Comprehensive Iranian guidelines for the diagnosis and management of maple syrup urine disease: an evidence- and consensus- based approach', vol. 20, article 8, published 7 January 2025, https://doi.org/10.1186/s13023-025-03533-6, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Daily leucine and protein needs by age (GMDI Table 4):** leucine 60–100 mg/kg under 3 months, 50–85 at 3–6 months, 35–70 at 6–12 months and 25–55 mg/kg from 1 to 4 years (total protein 2.5–3.0, 2.0–3.0, 2.0–2.5 and 1.5–2.1 g/kg); after 4 years in classical MSUD, 275–500 mg of leucine a day with total protein about 120% of the DRI. Classical MSUD tolerates the low end; adjust to plasma amino acids and growth.
claims.locator: Genetic Metabolic Dietitians International (GMDI) and the Southeast Regional Genetics Network (SERN), Management Guidelines Portal, 'MSUD Nutrition Management Guidelines, Second Edition (v2.1)', second edition October 2024, v2.1, updated March 2026, https://managementguidelines.net/guidelines.php/148/MSUD, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **S1's daily intakes for well patients (S1 Table 3), per kg:** 0–6 months leucine 40–100 mg, isoleucine 30–90 mg, valine 40–95 mg, protein 2.5–3.5 g, energy 95–145 kcal, fluid 125–160 mL; 7–12 months leucine 40–75 mg, protein 2.5–3.0 g; 1–3 years leucine 40–70 mg, protein 1.5–2.5 g; 4–8 years leucine 35–65 mg, protein 1.3–2.0 g; 9–13 years leucine 30–60 mg, protein 1.2–1.8 g; 14–18 years leucine 15–50 mg, protein 1.2–1.8 g; 19 years leucine 15–50 mg, protein 1.1–1.7 g.

claims.claim: **How often to measure leucine (GMDI Table 6):** daily until stable; in infants once or twice a week until 6 months, then weekly; in children 1 to under 8 years weekly until 24 months, then monthly; monthly in older children and adults; weekly in pregnancy and until 6 weeks postpartum.
claims.locator: Genetic Metabolic Dietitians International (GMDI) and the Southeast Regional Genetics Network (SERN), Management Guidelines Portal, 'MSUD Nutrition Management Guidelines, Second Edition (v2.1)', second edition October 2024, v2.1, updated March 2026, https://managementguidelines.net/guidelines.php/148/MSUD, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Offer a thiamine challenge to everyone** except those homozygous for the c.1312T>A variant or with other variants leaving under 3% enzyme activity: 50-200 mg/day, judged over one month on plasma BCAA and leucine tolerance. Responders stay on thiamine and a BCAA-restricted diet.
claims.locator: Genetic Metabolic Dietitians International (GMDI) and the Southeast Regional Genetics Network (SERN), Management Guidelines Portal, 'MSUD Nutrition Management Guidelines, Second Edition (v2.1)', second edition October 2024, v2.1, updated March 2026, https://managementguidelines.net/guidelines.php/148/MSUD, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Liver transplant (GMDI):** a valid option. Bring the candidate into good BCAA control first and prevent decompensation around surgery; after a successful transplant the diet can be relaxed and crisis precautions lifted, with dietetic support through the change.
claims.locator: Genetic Metabolic Dietitians International (GMDI) and the Southeast Regional Genetics Network (SERN), Management Guidelines Portal, 'MSUD Nutrition Management Guidelines, Second Edition (v2.1)', second edition October 2024, v2.1, updated March 2026, https://managementguidelines.net/guidelines.php/148/MSUD, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Pregnancy targets:** leucine 100-300 µM, valine and isoleucine at the upper end of normal (200-400µM). Leucine needs rise steeply: about 300-500 mg/day in the first trimester, 600-1000 in the second and 800-2000 in the third; return to pre-pregnancy intake after birth unless breastfeeding.
